- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
Search this repository very thoroughly for a server-push mechanism that sends live events to browsers. Look for:
1. SSE (Server-Sent Events), WebSocket, or similar real-time push mechanisms
2. A "hub" implementation that manages connections/subscriptions
3. Memo handlers that broadcast through this hub

Search for keywords: "SSE", "Server-Sent Events", "WebSocket", "hub", "broadcast", "EventSource", "text/event-stream", "pubsub", "event hub". Also look for files named hub.go, hub.ts, sse.go, etc.

Report: the mechanism type, the file path of the hub, and the names of memo handlers that broadcast through it.

content.text:
Here is the complete report of my findings.

---

## Server-Push Mechanism: SSE (Server-Sent Events)

**Mechanism type:** Server-Sent Events (SSE)

The repository implements a real-time push system using SSE -- not WebSockets. The server streams events over an HTTP connection with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, and the browser client consumes them using the Fetch API's streaming reader (not the native `EventSource` API).

---

### Hub Implementation

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`

The hub is the `SSEHub` struct (line 56). It is a concurrency-safe (via `sync.RWMutex`) connection manager with these core methods:

- `NewSSEHub()` -- constructor
- `Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient` -- registers a new SSE client with a buffered channel (capacity 32)
- `Unsubscribe(c *SSEClient)` -- removes a client and closes its channel
- `Broadcast(event *SSEEvent)` -- sends an event to all connected clients (with visibility-based filtering via `canReceive`; drops events for slow clients rather than blocking)
- `Close()` -- disconnects all clients (called on server shutdown)

The hub is instantiated in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` at line 57 as a field of `APIV1Service` (line 36: `SSEHub *SSEHub`), and is also referenced by the main server struct in `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (line 38).

---

### SSE HTTP Handler

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`

The endpoint is registered at `GET /api/v1/sse` (line 27). The handler:
1. Authenticates via Bearer token
2. Sets SSE headers (`text/event-stream`, `no-cache`, `keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`)
3. Subscribes to the hub
4. Sends an initial `: connected` comment
5. Loops, writing `data: <JSON>\n\n` for events and `: heartbeat\n\n` every 30 seconds

---

### Event Types

Defined in `sse_hub.go` (lines 14-21):

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `SSEEventMemoCreated` | `memo.created` |
| `SSEEventMemoUpdated` | `memo.updated` |
| `SSEEventMemoDeleted` | `memo.deleted` |
| `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated` | `memo.comment.created` |
| `SSEEventReactionUpserted` | `reaction.upserted` |
| `SSEEventReactionDeleted` | `reaction.deleted` |

---

### Memo/Reaction Handlers That Broadcast Through the Hub

Six broadcast call sites across four files:

1. **`CreateMemo`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (line 163)
   - Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoCreated` after a memo is created (suppressed when called internally from `CreateMemoComment` via context key `suppressSSEKey`).

2. **`DeleteMemo`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (line 585)
   - Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoDeleted` after a memo is deleted.

3. **`dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` (line 71)
   - Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoUpdated` after a memo is updated. This helper is called from `UpdateMemo` and related update paths.

4. **`CreateMemoComment`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` (line 126)
   - Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated` with the parent memo's name, so subscribers see the new comment.

5. **`UpsertMemoReaction`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go` (line 106)
   - Broadcasts `SSEEventReactionUpserted` via `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent`.

6. **`DeleteMemoReaction`** in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go` (line 161)
   - Broadcasts `SSEEventReactionDeleted` via `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent`.

---

### Helper for Reaction Events

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go`

Contains `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent` and `resolveSSECreatorID`, which construct the `SSEEvent` struct for reaction broadcasts, resolving the parent memo for visibility/creator filtering when the reaction is on a comment.

---

### Browser Client

**File:** `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts`

The React hook `useLiveMemoRefresh` connects to `/api/v1/sse` via `fetch` with streaming, parses the SSE data lines, and invalidates React Query caches based on the event type. It includes exponential-backoff reconnection (1s initial, 30s max) and exposes connection status via `useSSEConnectionStatus`. On reconnect, it invalidates all active memo queries to resync any events missed during disconnection.

---

### Test Files

- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub_test.go` -- unit tests for the hub (subscribe, unsubscribe, broadcast, private event scoping, slow client drop)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_service_test.go` -- integration tests verifying that service methods produce expected SSE events
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/sse_handler_test.go` -- HTTP-level tests for the SSE endpoint
